Two Stage Fixed Width Interval for a Negative Exponential Location

Source: R/ts_fwd_nexp_mean.R
ts_fwd_nexp_mean.Rd

Evaluates the two stage procedure for a confidence interval of fixed width for the location \(\theta\) of a negative exponential distribution: the model \(X = \theta + \sigma E\) with \(E\) a standard exponential variable, so that \(\theta\) is the smallest value the outcome can take (a threshold, a guarantee time, a minimum response time) and \(\sigma\) is the scale. Despite the function's name, the quantity estimated is the location \(\theta\), not the mean \(\theta + \sigma\). The first stage (pilot_data) fixes the total sample size; the second stage (additional_data) completes it. The interval is \([X_{(1)} - d,\ X_{(1)}]\), where \(X_{(1)}\) is the smallest of all observations from both stages and d is the full width.

Usage

ts_fwd_nexp_mean(
  pilot_data,
  additional_data = NULL,
  d,
  conf_level = 0.95,
  na.rm = TRUE
)

Arguments

pilot_data

Numeric vector of the first stage observations, at least two. The whole first stage must be supplied at every call, because it alone determines the total sample size.

additional_data

Numeric vector of the second stage observations collected so far, or NULL (the default) when none have been collected.

d

The full width of the confidence interval, in the units of the data. A single positive number.

conf_level

The confidence level, strictly between 0 and 1. Default 0.95.

na.rm

Logical. If TRUE (the default), missing values are removed from both stages before anything is computed; if FALSE, a missing value is an error.

Value

An object of class c("smsd_check", "data.frame") (see smsd_check_methods for its print(), summary(), and tidy() methods) with columns term and value and five rows:

lower_limit

\(X_{(1)} - d\), with \(X_{(1)}\) the smallest of all observations supplied.

location

\(X_{(1)}\), the estimate of \(\theta\).

upper_limit

\(X_{(1)}\); the interval is one-sided, so its upper limit is the estimate itself.

optimal_n

The total sample size \(N\) fixed by the first stage.

current_n

The number of observations supplied, both stages together.

Attributes: is_satisfied (TRUE once current_n is at least optimal_n), current_n, criterion_n (equal to optimal_n), conf_level, width (the full width d), method, and notes (always empty for this function). There is no variance_unusable attribute: a first stage whose scale cannot be estimated is an error (see Details).

Details

With \(m\) first stage observations, their minimum \(X_{(1:m)}\), and the scale estimate \(U_m = \sum_{i=1}^{m} (X_i - X_{(1:m)}) / (m - 1)\), the total sample size is $$N = \max\{m,\ \lceil F_{2,2m-2,\alpha} \, U_m / d \rceil\},$$ where \(F_{2,2m-2,\alpha}\) is the upper \(\alpha\) point of the F distribution with 2 and \(2m - 2\) degrees of freedom and \(\alpha = 1 - \) conf_level. If \(N = m\) the first stage is enough; otherwise \(N - m\) further observations are collected, once. \(N\) depends on the first stage alone. The row optimal_n is this total \(N\), not the number still to collect.

The quantile is one-sided because the interval is: the smallest observation can never fall below \(\theta\), so the interval misses only when \(X_{(1)} - \theta > d\).

The guarantee is exact. For negative exponential data the interval covers \(\theta\) with probability at least conf_level for every \(\theta\), every \(\sigma\), every d, and every first stage size \(m \ge 2\). (Given \(N\), the interval misses with probability \(\exp(-N d / \sigma)\); \(N\) depends only on \(U_m\), with \(2(m - 1) U_m / \sigma\) distributed as chi square on \(2m - 2\) degrees of freedom; and the expectation of \(\exp(-F U_m / \sigma)\) equals \(\alpha\) exactly at the F quantile used.) The price is sample size: the expected \(N\) is about \(F_{2,2m-2,\alpha} / \log(1/\alpha)\) times the known scale sample size \(C = \log(1/\alpha) \sigma / d\), which is why ts_fwd_nexp_mean_pilot does not return a very small first stage. The guarantee rests on the negative exponential model.

The interval rows are reported at every call so that progress can be followed, but the interval carries the stated confidence level only when the stopping rule is met, that is, when the current sample size has reached optimal_n.

A first stage with no variation is an error. If every first stage observation is equal, or equal up to rounding error (a range of no more than \(10^{-10}\) times the largest absolute value, the rule used throughout the package), the scale cannot be estimated and the function stops with an error that says what to do. The purely sequential functions report such data as a stopping rule that is not yet met, with the attribute variance_unusable; here that would mislead, because the total sample size is fixed by the first stage alone, so no later observation could turn a rule reported as not met into one that is met. Data whose real variation is that small beside their size (times recorded in seconds since 1970 that differ by hundredths of a second, for example) should have a common value subtracted from both stages first; the total sample size does not depend on it.

References

Mukhopadhyay, N., & de Silva, B. M. (2009). Sequential methods and their applications. Chapman & Hall/CRC. ISBN:9780367386535

See also

ts_fwd_nexp_mean_pilot for the first stage size; seq_fwd_nexp_mean for the purely sequential procedure.

Other ts_fwd_nexp_mean: ts_fwd_nexp_mean_pilot()

Author

Ken Kelley kkelley@nd.edu, Bhargab Chattopadhyay bhargab@iiitvadodara.ac.in

Examples

# A usability researcher models the time to complete a task as a
# shortest possible time plus an exponential delay, and wants the
# shortest possible time to within half a second, with 95% confidence.
set.seed(113)
m <- ts_fwd_nexp_mean_pilot(d = 0.5, conf_level = 0.95)
first_stage <- 3 + rexp(m, rate = 1 / 4)
check <- ts_fwd_nexp_mean(first_stage, d = 0.5)
check
#> Sequential check (two stage fixed width interval (negative exponential location))
#> 
#>   Current n       : 10
#>   Criterion n     : 29
#>   Target width    : 0.5
#>   Confidence level: 95%
#> 
#>   lower_limit       : 2.924348
#>   location          : 3.424348
#>   upper_limit       : 3.424348
#>   optimal_n         : 29
#>   current_n         : 10
#> 
#>   Stopping rule met: FALSE

# The first stage fixed the total sample size; collect the remainder.
n_more <- attr(check, "criterion_n") - attr(check, "current_n")
second_stage <- 3 + rexp(n_more, rate = 1 / 4)
ts_fwd_nexp_mean(first_stage, second_stage, d = 0.5)
#> Sequential check (two stage fixed width interval (negative exponential location))
#> 
#>   Current n       : 29
#>   Criterion n     : 29
#>   Target width    : 0.5
#>   Confidence level: 95%
#> 
#>   lower_limit       : 2.669607
#>   location          : 3.169607
#>   upper_limit       : 3.169607
#>   optimal_n         : 29
#>   current_n         : 29
#> 
#>   Stopping rule met: TRUE
